clue.text: Escort from falling house

definitions.meaning: an attendant who shows people to their seats in a theatre or church
Roderick, of Poe's tale The Fall of the House of ..., belongs to a family home that collapses

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a literary allusion: Edgar Allan Poe's story The Fall of the House of Usher ends with the mansion crumbling into a tarn.
explanation.definitionFit: An attendant who guides guests to seats, and the surname of the doomed family in Poe's story whose mansion falls.

clue.text: Free a French male, rescued somehow

parts.note: un is the masculine form of a in French

indicators.note: the letters of rescued are put in some other order

explanation.surface: Someone wants to free a Frenchman who has been rescued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' rearranges RESCUED to SECURED.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfastened or not tied down means loose.

clue.text: Assembling contents of the job lot, the lad makes such a fuss

indicators.note: takes the inner letter of each of the following short words

explanation.surface: A lad kicks up a row while sorting out a job lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contents of' takes the middle letter of THE, JOB, LOT, THE and LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A commotion or to-do is a row of excitement.

clue.text: Started firing again in part of army character commanded

parts.note: RE stands for Royal Engineers
kind means nature or character
led means commanded

explanation.surface: A unit of the army opens fire again under orders.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: To set alight once more is to start burning again.

clue.text: His best work is rarely picked

definitions.text: His best work is rarely picked

parts.words: His best work is rarely picked
parts.note: reads like a craftsman whose finest pieces are seldom chosen, but the tradesman's best mechanisms are those that resist picking by burglars

explanation.surface: A craftsman laments that his finest creations are seldom chosen by buyers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked' looks like 'chosen', but here it means opened with a pick: a good lock is one that burglars rarely manage to pick.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who makes secure fastenings for doors judges success by how seldom thieves can open them without a key.

clue.text: Rugby player is last in side to turn into hero

parts.note: a Lion plays for the British and Irish Lions touring rugby team

indicators.note: picks the final letter of the word side

explanation.surface: A rugby player at the end of the line becomes a hero.
explanation.walkthrough: The British and Irish Lions are a combined touring rugby side.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat a person as a celebrity is to make an idol of them.

clue.text: Arrived with something for sale in royal town

parts.note: came means arrived
a lot is an item at auction

explanation.surface: Arriving with goods to sell in a royal town.
explanation.walkthrough: Camelot is King Arthur's legendary court.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthurian legend places King Arthur's court in this town.

clue.text: Energy shown by second eleven

parts.note: a cricket or football side has eleven players

explanation.surface: A reserve side shows lots of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second eleven' suggests a reserve side, but splits into S and TEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Water vapour drives engines, and figuratively means vigour.

clue.text: Not to be trusted, in the main, since reckless

annotationWithheld.why: Not to be trusted, in the main, since reckless (9): IN + anagram of SINCE gives only seven letters; no word in 'the main' or 'reckless' supplies the remaining RE convincingly
annotationWithheld.clue: Not to be trusted, in the main, since reckless

clue.text: Group casting vote in poll

indicators.note: puts the vote mark within the word for poll

parts.note: the poll is an old word for the head
X is the mark cast on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A group casting its votes in an election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poll' looks like an election but is an old word for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of six is a group of that number.

clue.text: Standard accommodation, we hear, for capital city

indicators.note: signals that the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: standard means stock (regular, normal) and accommodation is a home, giving stock home

explanation.surface: Someone looks for ordinary lodgings in a big capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' turns STOCK HOME into a near-match for the Swedish capital when said out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swedish seat of government is a national capital.

clue.text: Former loved one, by Elizabeth beheaded

definitions.text: Former loved one, by Elizabeth beheaded

indicators.note: the pet name for Elizabeth loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: Bess is a familiar short form of Elizabeth
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: A historical note about a royal favourite executed on Elizabeth's orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beheaded' drops the first letter of Bess, a pet name for Elizabeth. Read whole, the clue describes Robert Devereux, Elizabeth I's favourite, executed in 1601.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earl bearing this title was Queen Elizabeth I's favourite and was executed for treason.

clue.text: Restrain murderer — put hothead inside

indicators.note: tells us to place one piece within the letters of the murderer's name

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis
the head, or first letter, of the word hot

explanation.surface: An order to subdue a killer and lock up a firebrand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hothead' looks like a rash person but gives just H, the first letter of 'hot'.
explanation.definitionFit: To shackle someone with linked metal is to restrain them.

clue.text: Stupid, dull men I repeatedly enlightened

indicators.note: used loosely to mean the letters are muddled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the letter I is used twice

explanation.surface: An insult about dim men followed by a claim of enlightenment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stupid' looks like an adjective about the men but signals an anagram of DULL MEN with I twice.
explanation.definitionFit: To be lit up mentally is to be illuminated, an older form of lit up.

clue.text: Determination to separate

definitions.meaning: to break something down into its component parts, as a mixture or a chord

explanation.definitionFit: The noun means steadfast purpose; the verb means to break into constituent parts, as in splitting light into colours.

clue.text: Severe on a marine using violence

parts.note: strong means harsh or severe
RM stands for Royal Marine

explanation.surface: A harsh treatment of a marine involving force.
explanation.walkthrough: RM is the abbreviation for the Royal Marines.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong-arm tactics are bullying, forceful ones.

clue.text: Bring back thick cheese in thin fabric

indicators.note: the word for thick is written backwards

parts.note: fat means thick or broad
feta is a Greek cheese

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction to wrap thick cheese in a fine cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring back' reverses FAT to TAF.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisp lustrous silk or synthetic weave is a light dress material.

clue.text: The best writing is based on direct experience

parts.note: first means best, top
a person's hand is their handwriting

explanation.surface: The top prose comes from personal experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand' is handwriting.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowledge gained directly, not via others, is direct.

clue.text: Expose important person it's okay to take off

parts.note: to air is to expose
a worthy is a notable person

explanation.surface: Exposing a VIP who is allowed to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' suggests leaving, but here means an aircraft becoming airborne.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft fit to fly has been passed safe for flight.

clue.text: Person who's contemptuous of French recommendation

parts.note: de is French for of
a rider is an added recommendation, as attached by a jury to a verdict

explanation.surface: Someone scornful of a French suggestion.
explanation.walkthrough: A rider is a clause or recommendation added to a verdict or report.
explanation.definitionFit: One who mocks or scorns treats others with contempt.

clue.text: Symbol of English house wines

parts.note: red is a type of wine
rose is a pink wine

explanation.surface: Wines of an English noble house.
explanation.walkthrough: The red rose is the emblem of the House of Lancaster, an English royal house.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lancastrians took the crimson bloom as their badge in the Wars of the Roses.

clue.text: Ancestor's decline

definitions.meaning: a forebear, someone from whom one is descended

explanation.definitionFit: Spelt this way it can be an older form of forebear, a forefather; as a verb it means hold back or refrain.

clue.text: Concentrates on coffee, initially, in blends

indicators.note: puts the following letters within the word for blends

parts.note: fuses means blends
O is a short form of on

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of the word coffee

explanation.surface: Someone focusing on coffee in blends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' places OC inside FUSES after the F.
explanation.definitionFit: Directs attention narrowly, as a lens does.

clue.text: Characters in Agen could blend this sort of wine

indicators.note: the letters are mixed as a winemaker blends grapes

explanation.surface: A remark that grapes from around Agen could be blended into a regional wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters in' points to the letters of AGEN COULD, which 'blend' rearranges. Agen is a town in south-west France.
explanation.definitionFit: The southern French region gives its name to a broad family of wines.

clue.text: Last character registered was a composer

annotationWithheld.why: Last character registered was a composer (5): Z inside LIST needs 'registered' both to give LIST and to signal the insertion, a word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Last character registered was a composer

clue.text: Various tunes still to be composed

indicators.note: the letters of tunes appear in another order

explanation.surface: Tunes yet to be written.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' signals an anagram of TUNES.
explanation.definitionFit: Not yet solidified or arranged means not set.

clue.text: At end of elephant, about trunk

indicators.note: picks the final letter of the word elephant

parts.note: or so means approximately

explanation.surface: Describes the rear of an elephant near its trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' suggests an elephant's nose, but it is the body without head or limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The human body minus head and limbs is called the trunk.

clue.text: Queen, say, with an evil princess

parts.note: R stands for Regina, queen
eg means for example

explanation.surface: A queen with a wicked princess.
explanation.walkthrough: Regan is one of the wicked daughters of King Lear.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's King Lear has a cruel daughter of this name.

clue.text: Strikes son with strap? Just the reverse

indicators.note: tells us to write the combination of son and strap backwards

parts.note: taws or tawse is a Scottish leather strap formerly used to punish pupils

explanation.surface: A father punishes his boy with a belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the reverse' turns S + TAWS round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Swipes or smacks sharply, as at a fly, are blows.

clue.text: Attack taking place — kill without hesitation

parts.note: something on is happening

indicators.note: tells us to remove the hesitation sound from the word for kill

parts.note: slaughter means kill
er is a hesitant sound

explanation.surface: An assault under way: kill without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' takes ER out of SLAUGHTER, leaving SLAUGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A fierce assault is a sweeping attack.

clue.text: Person occasionally working with hair, such as Delilah

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A part-time hairdresser, like the Delilah who cut Samson's hair.
explanation.walkthrough: Delilah seduced Samson and had his hair cut, a fitting reference given the hair in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Delilah is the biblical seductress who lured Samson, an example of an enticing woman.

clue.text: Dorothy's skirts are so smart

indicators.note: the outside letters go round another word, as a skirt goes round

parts.note: first and last letters of Dorothy
so can mean and, as in so it goes on

explanation.surface: Dorothy's skirts are very fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and last letters of Dorothy, D and Y, 'skirt' AND.
explanation.definitionFit: A dandy is a fop; as an adjective it means fine, stylish.
